newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada farmers pay more to do business in Q1/97.
newsitem.headline: Canada farmers pay more to do business in Q1/97.

text.p: Canadian farmers paid 2.4 percent more to do business in the first quarter of 1997 compared to the first quarter in 1996, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
The rise was despite a 13.2 percent decline in interest costs, the federal agency said.
StatsCan said Western Canadian farmers, particularly those who raise livestock, paid more to do business over the past 12 months than their counterpats in the East.
In the first quarter of 1997, farm input prices for Western Canada rose 2.9 percent from the same period a year earlier, compared with only a 1.8 percent increase for Eastern Canada, the agency said.
The farm input price index rose 0.9 percent to 128.4 in the first quarter of 1997 compared to 127.3 in the fourth quarter of 1996, the agency said.

For western farmers, the price of virtually all inputs into animal production increased 8.9 percent in the quarter compared to the first quarter of 1996, while in the east, it went up only 2.5 percent.

The first quarter figures are the only ones to reflect changes in the farm rent and property tax indexes, StatsCan said. At the national level, the index for farm rent declined 1.8 percent, while the property tax index increased 3.6 percent.
